We are now less than 50 days from the midterm elections and if Pennsylvania Gov. Josh Shapiro wants to see his dream of the Democratic trifecta in Harrisburg come true, his party has to hold the governor’s mansion and its majority in the State House, while flipping the majority in the state Senate.

Republicans currently hold a 27-23 advantage in the chamber, but Democrats are hopeful that party enthusiasm and Republican disenchantment with the national GOP could enable Dems to take the effective control of the chamber with a 25-25 tie for the first time since 1992. The last year that Democrats held the outright majority was 1978.

To make that control a reality, Democrats must win at least two races while retaining the two seats it currently holds.

Pennsylvania State Senate election results: 1992-2024

source: Ballotpedia

With 25 races on the docket, we decided to focus on races that:

  • Had a district voter registration margin of 10 points or less
  • District was won by Trump or Harris by 10 points or less
  • The margin of victory was four (4) points or less in the last election

SD-6 (Bucks County): Frank Farry (R) v. Eileen Hartnett Albillar (D)
VR: R+4.78 | 2024: Trump +5 | Farry 53-45

SD-16 (Bucks, Lehigh): Jarrett Coleman (R) v. Mark Pinsley (D)
VR: R+11 | 2024: Trump +9 | Coleman d. Pinsley 54-46

SD-24 (Berks, Montgomery): Tracy Pennycuick (R) v. Chris Thomas (D) and Michael Schonewolf (G)
VR: R+6 | 2024: Trump +2 | Pennycuick 52-48

SD-36 (Lancaster): James Malone (D) v. Tom Jones (R)
VR: R+22 | 2024: Trump +15 | Malone 50-49 (526 votes) in 2025 special

SD-40 (Lackawanna, Monroe, Wayne): Rosemary Brown (R) v. Brian Wrightson (D)
VR: D+1.24 | 2024: Trump +6 | Brown 55-45

SD-44 (Berks, Chester, Montgomery): Katie Muth (D) v. Melissa Dicranian (R)
VR: D+0.44 | 2024: Harris +11 | Muth 56-44
